name: Purplish Pink
lede: Purplish Pink is a deep orchid pink, the standard-spelling twin of [[pale-magenta]] from the same 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: The standard spelling of a compound
sections.body:
As with its blue counterpart, the survey kept both "purplish" and "purpleish" forms over pink, so this name and [[pale-magenta]] are near-duplicates, 5.3 units apart [1]. No earlier dictionary or dye name is documented for either; 2010 is the only source on file [1]. The ISCC-NBS system would place it among the deep purplish pinks, 7.3 units off [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[pale-magenta]], 3.5 units away and almost the same shade [2]. [[mulberry-crayola]] sits close behind, also nearly the same, with [[pinky-purple]] and [[frostbite]] further off and more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our full-canvas search finds no match in the 23,781-painting archive, but a narrower, within-painting search turns up a single trace, as photographed [3]. That single trace puts it rarer than 86 percent of our named colors by that measure [3]. One painting is too thin a record to draw a pattern from [3].
